name: recall checker

product.purpose: Check reseller inventory against current public recalls and provide the official notice for review.
channels: thrift and consignment store inventory CSV
product.publication: Recall pages are generated locally. The owner reviews the first 50 and submits any Chrome Web Store listing; no page or extension is published automatically.
product.billing: Individual and store plan ranges and a free single-lookup tier are in plans.json. The owner configures Stripe test prices before checkout links are offered; API metering is not activated until the owner sets a price.

schedules.purpose: Refresh recall feeds and rebuild local, source-linked recall pages.

your_steps.title: Review the first 50 recall pages and choose a host
your_steps.when: Ready now; before any public release
your_steps.detail: Review the prepared first 50 source-linked local pages in evidence/first-50-pages/, verify each recall number, date and official notice link, and record corrections. Choose and configure a public host only if you want the pages public. Public release remains gated on the independent fuzzy-match review. Exact steps and time estimate are in OWNER-STEPS.md.

your_steps.title: Publish the prepared Actor and extension listings
your_steps.when: After the source and verification gates pass
your_steps.detail: Rename the deployed Product Recall Checker Actor to Glacier Product Recall Checker, review its run limit and choose its final price (the prepared portfolio table suggests $0.01 per recall-check), then publish the Actor listing. Upload the prepared extension ZIP, paste the copy-ready listing and privacy disclosures, review the permissions and submit it for Chrome Web Store review. Exact clicks and the prepared assets are in OWNER-STEPS.md and store/STORE-LISTING.md. Paid plans and Stripe setup are deferred until you choose exact plan prices.

launch_gates: The official FSIS JSON API canary returns records with the expected recall identifier and all four live recall snapshots are current and alert-free before a no-match result or recall pages are treated as complete.
The 500-known-recalled and 500-known-clean NHTSA vehicle benchmark remains at or below 1% false no-match before an update is released.
Independent second-engine review for fuzzy matches is complete; borderline outcomes remain uncertain until then.
The owner reviews the first 50 recall pages before public hosting.
The owner submits the first Chrome Web Store listing and configures the selected test prices.
